families.title: Read three-dimensional positions from a stated coordinate frame
families.learner_decisions: Locate the origin and positive axes,then translate each labelled vertex/midpoint into its coordinates.
families.givens_and_unknowns: Cuboid,cube or prism with axis directions and dimensions; unknown labelled positions or directed displacements.
families.constraints: Centred cube coordinates use half-side lengths;translated cubes retain the stated offset. Every label must remain incident with the correct source edge/face.
families.representation_and_response: Given3Ddiagram to coordinate tuples and requested vectors.
families.scaffolding_and_connected_parts: One shared coordinate model governs allvertices;midpoint questions reuse it.
families.alternative_methods: Axis-aligned coordinate reconstruction and midpoint arithmetic;vector differences for requested arrows.
families.units_and_precision: Keep exact radicals,ratios and cosine expressions unless a member asks a decimal angle/length. Distinguish3sf,2dp,1dpandnearest degree. A direction from+x,a bearing and an acute angle between lines have different conventions;use the original request.
families.answer_form: Every requested labelled tuple/vector,not an unlabeled set.
families.difficulty_progression: YM1starts at a corner;2centres the cube;Try1(b)translates it and has a copied key;GoldieActivity1adds five edge midpoints and multiple equal displacements.
families.distinction_basis: Choosing the frame is a learner decision;numeric side changes alone are ordinary variation.

families.givens_and_unknowns: Two/three-dimensional vector or a specified vector difference; unknown magnitude.
families.constraints: Magnitude nonnegative;zero vector has magnitudezeroeven though it has no direction. Unit cases remain exact.
families.representation_and_response: Component/basis vector to exact radical or requested rounded scalar.
families.scaffolding_and_connected_parts: A difference may be required before its norm;no direction is inferred from magnitude alone.
families.alternative_methods: Euclidean norm or Pythagoras on successive orthogonal components.
families.units_and_precision: Keep exact radicals,ratios and cosine expressions unless a member asks a decimal angle/length. Distinguish3sf,2dp,1dpandnearest degree. A direction from+x,a bearing and an acute angle between lines have different conventions;use the original request.
families.answer_form: Requested scalar length with units if supplied.
families.difficulty_progression: Goldie3asks2dp;YM3contains already-unit vectors and zero components;Try7Q4first forms a signed difference.
families.distinction_basis: Norm computation is not normalisation or scalar product.

families.difficulty_progression: YM6has two unknowns;Try6Q2uses opposite factor-2and its key sign is wrong;Try16Q2contrasts parallel and perpendicular requests.

families.title: Prove collinearity,parallel sides or bisection from vector relations
families.learner_decisions: Form the required directed vectors,show a shared scalar relation and state the geometric conclusion with its common-point/incidence condition.
families.givens_and_unknowns: Position vectors or labelled triangle/parallelogram/cuboid with midpoints; unknown vectors and geometric proof.
families.constraints: Parallel vectors alone do not establish collinearity without a shared point;equal diagonal midpoints justify bisection,not arbitrary diagonal length equality.
families.representation_and_response: Diagram/algebra input to vector expressions and reasoned proof.
families.scaffolding_and_connected_parts: Preliminary vectors are reused in the proof. Source geometric labels remain fixed across all parts.
families.alternative_methods: Vector differences,affine midpoint identities or equivalent coordinate proofs with explicit conclusion.
families.units_and_precision: Keep exact radicals,ratios and cosine expressions unless a member asks a decimal angle/length. Distinguish3sf,2dp,1dpandnearest degree. A direction from+x,a bearing and an acute angle between lines have different conventions;use the original request.
families.answer_form: Asked vectors plus complete geometric justification.
families.difficulty_progression: Goldie10B5proves midpoint-triangle properties;10B11uses positions to prove a parallelogram;YM9/Try9contain nontrivial directed external relations.
families.distinction_basis: A geometric proof needs a conclusion and incidence evidence beyond correct component arithmetic.

families.scaffolding_and_connected_parts: Area/perimeter outputs remain distinct from the preliminary angle;source exactness requirements retained.

families.units_and_precision: Keep exact radicals,ratios and cosine expressions unless a member asks a decimal angle/length. Distinguish3sf,2dp,1dpandnearest degree. A direction from+x,a bearing and an acute angle between lines have different conventions;use the original request.

families.difficulty_progression: Goldie11asksQPR;YM18proves exactcos=1/3thenarea10√2;Try18Q2asksOABrather thanAOB.

insights.title: Coordinate frames,notation and geometric vector operations
insights.teaching_comparison: YM begins with corner,centred and translated solids before vector notation,magnitude and operations. Goldie begins with2Ddirection/grid reading,then extends to3Dmagnitudes and cuboid/regular-prism routes. Both develop internal ratios,midpoints and collinearity proofs. Goldie’s formal vector-line sections exceed8227scope,but explicitly retained supplied-relation or Cartesian-accessible facets remain useful internal evidence.
insights.examination_comparison: NSSCAS2023P1Q7(a)(i)(ii)uses joining vectors;2024P1Q10(a)(b)requires3Ddiagram reading before vectors. Textbooks add centred/translated frames,regular-hexagonal bases and longer midpoint proofs. The defective2021P1Q6external division remains held;GoldieExample12(iii)independently illustrates why an unsigned ratio may yield an external point as well.
insights.difficulty_and_grade_bounds: E07/A07name3Dcoordinates/notation;C07names addition,subtraction,scaling and geometric interpretation. Difficulty increases through frame choice,label incidence and proof connections,not simply a third nonzero component. A supplied affine identity is not permission to author arbitrary formal vector-line equations.
insights.pitfalls: YMTry1(b)copies the wrong prism’s coordinates;Try6Q2has an opposite-direction sign error. GoldieExample12(iii)omits the external ratio point. Equal vector directions alone do not prove point collinearity unless the vectors share the relevant point. These are registered source/author cautions,not claims of examiner-error frequency.
insights.gaps_and_representations: Both books support routine component operations;Goldie offers a regular-prism symbolic basis,YM centred-coordinate practice. Generated diagrams will need consistent vertex frames and head/tail labels. Supporting motion/locus tasks with supplied relations do not establish additional prescribed formal-line coverage.
insights.implications_for_step3: Propose explicit origin,basis,orientation and directed-endpoint data,with independent reconstruction of every vertex. Retain internal/external ratio branches and require the geometric conclusion in proofs. Keep scope decisions at named-part level so useful prescribed operations survive an otherwise excluded chapter.

insights.title: Magnitude,unit vectors and sign of parallel direction
insights.teaching_comparison: Both books compute norms before unit vectors and derived positions. YM4asks a unit vector PARALLELwhile later5specifies SAMEdirection;Goldie10B6/7explicitlynormalises given directions and10B12first derives an external point. Source examples displaying only a positive normalisation do not remove the negative answer when wording merely saysparallel.
insights.examination_comparison: The mapped NSSCAS2021–2025sample has no usable direct unit-vector part. Unit vectors remain syllabus-required and textbook-supported;this is a genuine sampled gap,not an exclusion. Norms also occur inside exam angle/spatial chains,which do not automatically directly assess unit normalisation.
insights.difficulty_and_grade_bounds: E07/C07name unit,displacement and position vectors;A07names magnitude. Increased demand comes from deriving the target vector,selecting a direction sign or satisfying a requested nonunit magnitude. The zero vector must be invalid for normalisation even though its norm calculation is valid.
insights.pitfalls: YMExercise5Q1unit key has one wrong sign;Q6key supplies an unnormalised diagonal. Other suspected signs were cleared on native renders,includingExercise5Q5’snegative middle component. Independent checks should verify norm ANDparallel/direction,not merely compare printed components. No examiner-specific unit-vector error rate is claimed.
insights.gaps_and_representations: Both books give extensive direct unit practice despite no sampled NSSCASdirect part. Parallel-only versus same-direction needs an answer-policy branch. A normalised joining vector and a raw joining vector are distinct outputs even when they share a source label.
insights.implications_for_step3: Propose nonzero norm constraints,explicit parallel versus same-direction wording and acceptance of both signs where warranted. Recover geometric points before normalisation and check the original unit/length condition independently. Preserve this syllabus-derived practice in planning rather than dropping it for lack of sampled exams.

insights.title: Scalar products,angle conventions and perpendicular parameters
insights.teaching_comparison: YM pairs magnitude-angle and component definitions of the scalar product,then contrasts angle,parallel and perpendicular conditions. Goldie asks explicit proof/assumption prompts and develops obtuse/opposite vectors before spatial angle problems. Both later solve parameterised angle and length conditions. The common-vertex choice and angle convention are retained,not hidden inside an acosformula.
insights.examination_comparison: NSSCAS2023P1Q7(b)(i)(ii),2024P1Q10(c)and2025P1Q3anchor vector-angle/perpendicular reasoning. ERR09explicitly supports zero scalar product for perpendicular vectors. Textbook polar directions,bearings,acute line angles and diagram elevation are distinct conventions. Formal skew-line tasks are not imported merely because their directions can supply supporting dot practice.
insights.difficulty_and_grade_bounds: C07/A07include scalar-product angles and perpendicularity. Extra difficulty is choosing the two correct arms,constructing a spatial model,or checking unsquared sign after a parameter equation. Opposite vectors give180degrees;an acute line angle instead uses the specifically requested convention. Grade descriptions do not justify replacing every angle by its acute supplement.
insights.pitfalls: Goldie10F10requires rejecting a squared-equation root with the wrong cosine sign;YM16andTry18Q1preserve valid correlated signs. A perpendicularity equation may have no real parameter when the dot is25+p². ERR09corroborates the orthogonality principle;the exact squared-angle traps remain textbook/author cautions rather than reported learner frequencies.
insights.gaps_and_representations: Both books offer direct given-vector angles and richer diagrams. Roof/cube/pyramid reconstruction adds geometry before the same final dot calculation;these must not collapse into a routine component pair. A polar direction measured from+xdoesnot assess the same response as a three-point angle.
insights.implications_for_step3: Propose explicit angle vertex/reference,nonzero arms,original cosine sign and precision. Use independently computed dot/norm and reconstructed solid coordinates to verify every angle. Retain impossibility and two-parameter-branch cases deliberately;match source method instructions rather than infer official marks from a worked example.
